advisor_identified: Historian of Russian and modern European history at the University of Saskatchewan; supervisor of Rob Morley’s 2014 history PhD.

evidence.says: Lists Morley, Rob, PhD, defence January 14, 2014, supervisor J. McCannon, and The Screen's Threatening Skies: Aerial Warfare and British Cinema, 1927-1939.

Canadian Historical Association Bulletin 37.1 (2011), PDF page 34, identifies John McCannon as an associate professor of Russian and modern European history at Saskatchewan and explicitly gives his PhD as University of Chicago, 1994.

University of Michigan OLLI speaker biography identifies McCannon as a historian of Russia and the polar regions, gives Chicago as his MA/PhD institution, and records teaching at Saskatchewan and authorship of Red Arctic (1998).

Red Arctic (Oxford University Press, 1998), acknowledgments p. v, read in a licensed publisher preview: McCannon states that the book grew directly from his graduate research, names his dissertation committee at Chicago, and dates the final stage of dissertation work to 1993-1994.

notes: The linked AHA record matches the independently confirmed institution and year, and its Red Arctic subject matches McCannon’s documented dissertation-derived book. Exact dissertation title was not independently verified in a library or repository catalogue, so title is null; the book has a different subtitle.
